producer_report.summary:
I rewrote docs/design/parallel-jobs.md to answer review 1 (F1-F8). The status stays "proposed", with the revision awaiting a second review. A table at the top maps each finding to the section that answers it. I also made a short edit to the roadmap's parallel-jobs line and added a CHANGELOG entry under a new "Changed" heading. No code changed.

- **F1:** The design drops the claim that disjoint jobs land through local replay. `plan` replays a candidate only over records-only changes, so any sibling's governed change makes a job stale. Each job now lands through its own pull request by squash, and the local branch is rebuilt on the merged commit after each landing (cites native-pr-landing.md §5.2a and §5.7). Landings go through a queue one at a time. A job whose base is behind the new HEAD is stale, or `merged-unverified` if the host merged it anyway. It leaves that state only through a user-requested re-verify as a new budgeted job. §7, §8, the build order and question 2 are rewritten.
- **F2:** One child process per job is the default. Threads are not chosen because `AgentDriver` and `Ui` have no Send or Sync bound and a caught panic is not enough isolation. A spike would have to show four things, listed in the document. The process model covers spawning, collecting output and exit codes, and the kill switch.
- **F3:** New section 9 on shared append-only files. Only a docs job that runs alone writes them, and it allocates decision numbers at write time. Jobs that name the same file are serialized. The section has a table of what the landing check enforces versus what is a hint, and a four-point collision test.
- **F4-F8:**
  - Duplicate refs are rejected after resolving to ids.
  - The kill-switch check comes before the job lock.
  - The worst-case spend (N times the per-job cap) is printed at the start of a run.
  - Line references were re-read and corrected to run.rs 698, land_or_block from 1165, and retry_landing from 1344 with its loop at 1424-1433. The Ui and Athena lines in lib.rs had drifted to 56 and 69.
  - The seven open questions are settled, plus two new ones carried forward with stated decisions.

open_issues: Whether the user-requested re-verify of a stale job (native-pr-landing §5.7) is built was not checked. The design says the build must confirm it.
The budget code (run.rs 182-240), gh.rs lock order, and the configured value of job_usd were not re-read; the design labels these as unchecked.
The 'processes start in a few milliseconds' claim and the default of 2 workers with a ceiling of 4 are estimates, not measurements, and are labeled so in the design.
mistakes: The roadmap and CHANGELOG edits were not strictly required for a design-only change. I made them because the expected deliverables list them and the roadmap text said 'apply its changes'.
learnings: The native-pr-landing flow pushes the job's locally landed commit, so local landing still happens before the pull request. The pool must therefore queue landings one at a time. This is carried forward as question 8.
The review's line numbers for lib.rs had drifted: Ui is at 56 and Athena at 69. The run.rs lines (698, 1165, 1424) were still correct.
main.rs enters prompt_loop only when stdin and stdout are both terminals, so piped child processes never prompt.

gh.rs line 611 is a third try_lock_job caller (land --pr). The lock-order argument depends on it taking the repository lock only after its job lock. I did not verify that, and it is carried forward as question 9.
desires: A way to run `git diff --stat` output in the brief's allowed commands without it being unclear whether untracked files show
